claim: You can create an Athena table automatically with an AWS Glue crawler. When AWS Glue creates a table, it registers it in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, which Athena uses to store and retrieve metadata.

Athena uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to store and retrieve this metadata, using it when you run queries to analyze the underlying dataset.

claim: Athena does not recognize exclude patterns set on an AWS Glue crawler, so it queries all files in the S3 location, including the ones the crawler excluded.
question: Does Athena honor the exclude patterns of a Glue crawler?

values.display: Athena does not recognize exclude patterns
Athena queries both groups of files

qualifiers.condition: place files to exclude in a different location

evidence.quote: Athena does not recognize exclude patterns that you specify for an AWS Glue crawler. For example, if you have an Amazon S3 bucket that contains both .csv and .json files and you exclude the .json files from the crawler, Athena queries both groups of files. To avoid this, place the files that you want to exclude in a different location.

claim: Athena can query restored S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive objects only if you enable the capability on a per-table basis. Without it, Athena skips all of the table's Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive objects during query execution.

values.display: enable the capability on a per-table basis

evidence.quote: You can use Athena to query restored objects from the Amazon Glacier Flexible Retrieval (formerly Glacier) and Amazon Glacier Deep Archive Amazon S3 storage classes but you must enable the capability on a per-table basis. If you do not enable the feature on a table before you run a query, Athena skips all of the table's Amazon Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Amazon Glacier Deep Archive objects during query execution.
